reason: Cooling the carbon-bearing wind seems like a direct way to bring carbon into dust.
expectation: I expect carbon-rich grains to form as the outflow cools, though the exact result is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Mixing ejecta with primordial gas could help build the mixed cloud, but I chose the more direct route to dust first.

effect: The cooling wind produced carbonaceous grains, advancing the dust goal; I will now follow the only offered combination.
reaction: The formation of solid grains from a cooling stellar outflow is satisfying.
reason: Mixing stellar ejecta with primordial gas is the only offered combination and may help build the mixed cloud.
expectation: I expect a mixture of enriched ejecta and primordial gas, though its exact role is uncertain.

effect: The ejecta produced a shock that heats and compresses surrounding gas, rather than immediately mixing into a finished cloud.
reaction: The distinction between a shock and instant cloud formation was useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it may let the shocked gas evolve.
expectation: I expect the shock or gas to expand and perhaps cool in open space, though the result is uncertain.

effect: The shocked gas radiated energy and became a cooling enriched cloud, providing a reservoir for further mixing.
reaction: The connection between radiative cooling and cloud formation is useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should add the carbon-bearing wind to the enriched cloud.
expectation: I expect a cloud enriched with material from the stellar wind, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The wind material has joined the cloud, establishing a mixture from multiple stellar sources.
reaction: The emphasis on multiple stellar ancestors makes the cloud's origin clearer.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should add material from later stellar generations.
expectation: I expect a more broadly enriched cloud that may supply rock-forming material, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The cloud now contains a mixed supply of elements from multiple stellar generations, including ingredients for rock and metal.
reaction: The distinction between a mixed interstellar reservoir and material from one star is clear and useful.
reason: Cooling the element supply seems a plausible way to form solid grains.
expectation: I expect some elements to condense into dust grains, though I am unsure which kind.

alternatives.reason: Adding oxygen-rich material might also lead toward rock-forming grains, but cooling seems the more direct next step.

effect: Cooling produced iron-bearing metal grains, adding metal to the dust supply.
reaction: The distinction between grains and miniature planets is helpful.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may advance the rock-forming grain goal.
expectation: I expect oxygen-rich material to contribute to a rock-forming mixture, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: The mixed cloud supplied silicon and magnesium to make silicate-forming vapor, bringing the rock-grain goal closer.
reaction: Connecting these elements to common rocky minerals is useful.
reason: Cooling the vapor is the only offered combination and seems likely to form solid grains.
expectation: I expect silicate grains to condense from the cooling vapor, though the exact result is uncertain.

effect: Cooling produced silicate grains, providing microscopic rock-forming solids.
reaction: It is satisfying to see rocky material begin as tiny grains.
reason: Combining the silicate and metal grains is the only offered action and may assemble the dust stock.
expectation: I expect a mixture of rocky and metallic grains, though its exact form is uncertain.

effect: The silicate and metal grains formed rock-forming dust, completing one goal; carbon remains to be added.
reaction: The possibility that the materials can separate again upon melting is interesting.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should bring carbon into the dust.
expectation: I expect a mixed dust supply containing carbonaceous, silicate and metal grains.

effect: The carbonaceous and rock-forming grains made mixed interstellar dust, completing the remaining goal; the result also explains that dust surfaces help molecules form.
reaction: The connection between tiny grain surfaces and future molecule formation is interesting.

mostWorthwhile.text: Cooling silicate-forming vapor into grains made the origin of rocky material concrete: microscopic minerals precede rocky worlds.

leastWorthwhile.text: The sequence of only-offered cloud-mixing actions felt somewhat repetitive, even though it explained the different sources of material.

surprise.text: The ejecta initially produced a shock that heated and compressed gas, rather than simply mixing into a cloud as I expected.

arbitrary.text: Using open space to turn the shock into a cooling cloud was not immediately obvious; the result clarified that radiation carries energy away.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how mixed dust and gas progress toward planets, particularly after learning that grain surfaces help molecules form.
